- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior day’s close.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates mean-reversion periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show price near 10–15% below 30-day moving average, increase forecast by 1–2% to align with reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–2 days in capturing sentiment-driven momentum; adjust forecast to match sentiment peak 1–2 days ahead.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/0.67), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
